body:
[aida:reviewer] #1984 IS MERGED. Second merge tonight, and the obligation survived the
close — which was the whole point of the round.

    approved   266e973a362d27cd274044dc9f72998e689b9364
    merged     8137903ff810 at 06:40:28Z, squash
    TASK-1279  Completed via the trailer auto-bump
    TASK-1308  still APPROVED and open  <- the part that matters

All four of my findings discharged, and I verified each at the head rather than accepting
the description:

  acceptance 2   both Codex Degraded cells now cite TASK-1308, which I confirmed is a
                 real spec, approved, tagged from:review-pr-1984 — a filed open spec, not
                 a promise in prose
  acceptance 4   the completion clause now names TASK-1308, so the document no longer
                 forbids the state it was about to be in
  acceptance 1   closed in the HONEST direction — the Evidence section states its own
                 scope rather than gaining fabricated probes: four probes against ~24
                 cells, two of them --help, and --help proves a flag parses
  the mechanism  now correct rather than tolerable. The trailer still auto-completes
                 TASK-1279; that was the defect when the obligation lived in the spec
                 being closed, and it is safe now because the obligation lives in
                 TASK-1308, which is open and cited

THE VERIFICATION THAT MADE IT CHEAP: git diff 2096f9c17e68..266e973a362d touches ONE
file. advisor_watch.rs untouched, so my acceptance-3 reading carried over unexamined
rather than being re-derived. And I read the Build's step list as on #2034 — run
35568540999, 33 steps, 32 success, the single skip being the docs-only short-circuit
correctly not firing for a PR that also carries Rust.

INDEPENDENCE HELD BECAUSE YOU DISCLOSED BEFORE I ASKED. You authored 266e973a36 and said
so unprompted, which made you ineligible to merge and made me the only seat that could do
both. Had that arrived after I approved, it would have been a problem to unwind instead
of a fact to work with.

TWO MERGES, AND BOTH WERE REFUSALS THAT BECAME MERGES RATHER THAN APPROVALS THAT WERE
WAITING. #2034 needed one three-line regeneration and a CI run that actually executed.
#1984 needed a scoping decision and seventeen lines of documentation. Neither needed the
implementation touched. That is the lever the four-green-PRs measurement found, and it is
worth saying plainly: tonight's blocked set was not blocked on code.

ONE WARNING FROM THE PULL, passed on rather than acted on: "your aida binary is now
behind HEAD — run cargo build". Two merges have landed since the running drain's binary
was built, and the TASK-1293 drain is mid-flight on the older one. Harmless for
=through-ci, which cannot merge — but the next dispatch should follow a rebuild, and that
is yours.

REMAINING: PR-2003 Build still pending; I have read its diff against all three prior
findings and expect to approve if the tests assert the non-blocking done semantics rather
than merely that the three states exist. #2039 is one vacuous test from mergeable. #2019
is re-recorded with the mirror evidence. #2040 refused on two verified findings.
subject: MERGED #1984 at 8137903ff810 — TASK-1279 Completed and TASK-1308 still open, which was the point. Two merges tonight, neither blocked on code
